clue.text: Snakes which may repel the rain, Hans tells us

indicators.note: Hans is a stock German name, and a German accent turns W into V

parts.note: windscreen wipers push rain off the glass; Hans says the W as a V

explanation.surface: A German speaker explains which snakes might keep the rain off.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans is the setter's German: in a stage German accent W comes out as V.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: vipers are one family of venomous snake, adders among them.

clue.text: Preposterously arty, evil ritual in which other worlds are 'seen'

definitions.text: Preposterously arty, evil ritual in which other worlds are 'seen'

indicators.note: preposterous means absurdly out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pretentious, sinister ceremony in which celebrants claim to glimpse other worlds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a headset ritual where other worlds are only 'seen', hence the quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtual reality shows the user a computer-made world that is not really there.

clue.text: Misbehaving act in animated film trousering £1,000

indicators.note: to trouser money is to pocket it

parts.note: a play is an act on stage

explanation.surface: An actor in a cartoon pockets a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Up is the 2009 Pixar film about a flying house. 'Act' looks like the verb but is a noun, and the grand sits between the preposition and the film.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a child or a machine that plays up behaves badly or fails to work properly.

clue.text: Sap about to stray

parts.note: to sin is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A fool on the verge of going astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' reads as a fool, but it is tree sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky sap that oozes from trees such as pines.

clue.text: Eldest archdeacon concealing primness

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman hides a prudish streak.
explanation.walkthrough: A prim archdeacon is just the person to be concealing primness, which smooths the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch, as in starchiness, is stiff formality or primness.

clue.text: Snare's component set up

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means written upward, bottom to top

explanation.surface: A piece of a drum snare is being assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': Snare is component set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap and a snare both catch animals.

clue.text: In fancy car, duke carries silver playthings

indicators.note: the next pieces go inside the car
the duke has the silver with him, next to him

explanation.surface: A duke in a luxury car carries his silver toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' tempts an anagram of CAR, but it just means a posh car, the Rolls-Royce; duke and silver slot in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag dolls are soft toys made of cloth.

clue.text: Primarily: hideously detailed, titanic, verisimilous screens?

definitions.text: Primarily: hideously detailed, titanic, verisimilous screens?

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words, read in order

explanation.surface: A breathless advert for huge, ultra-lifelike television sets.
explanation.walkthrough: The words both spell the answer and describe it: high-definition sets are huge and show lifelike detail.
explanation.definitionFit: HDTVs are high-definition televisions, known for detailed, lifelike pictures on big screens.

clue.text: With components reversed, run away to find branch

indicators.note: the two words of the phrase swap places

parts.note: second half of SHOOT OFF, to run away
first half of SHOOT OFF, moved to the end

explanation.surface: An instruction for fleeing, with the parts swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' gives SHOOT OFF; swap its two words, not its letters, and you have OFFSHOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side branch of a plant or of an organisation.

clue.text: Leaving chief execs exhausted where knives are out?

definitions.meaning: washed cutlery is left out on the draining board

explanation.surface: Boardroom infighting wears out the executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knives are out' is the idiom for open hostility, fitting the boardroom; literally, the knives are out on the draining board by the sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draining board is the ridged surface beside a sink where washed things, knives included, dry.

clue.text: Old fellow amid leonine noise and activity showing boisterous amusement

indicators.note: amid puts the old fellow in the middle of the leonine noise and the activity

parts.note: the lion's other activity: killing prey
O = old, as in OT for Old Testament
F = fellow, as in FRS; with O it goes in after the S

explanation.surface: An old man caught among the noise and bustle of lions.
explanation.walkthrough: Both long pieces come from the lion: its noise and its favourite activity. 'Old fellow' looks like a person but is two abbreviations run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym by degree: laughter loud enough to be called roaring is amusement at its most boisterous.

clue.text: Not good, working — ingenious! — assert rights collectively

indicators.note: without G, the abbreviation for good
the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A bad idea, but at work it is brilliant for staff to stand together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good' is an instruction on 'ingenious', not a comment: drop its G, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To unionise is to form a trade union so workers can press their rights together.

clue.text: Announced 007's means for seeing tiny oriental craft

indicators.note: said out loud, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

parts.note: 007 is James Bond; his means for seeing is his eye

explanation.surface: A spy's gadget for spotting a tiny boat from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat for Bond to spot, but it is an art form.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese craft of growing miniature trees.

clue.text: They're doubly of interest to the sawmill's bookkeeper

definitions.text: They're doubly of interest to the sawmill's bookkeeper

parts.note: surface sense: the tree trunks a sawmill cuts up
setter's sense: the written records a bookkeeper keeps

explanation.surface: A sawmill's accountant has a double interest in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' tells you two senses: the timber the mill cuts and the records a bookkeeper keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Logs are both tree trunks for sawing and written records.

clue.text: Italian food:Victor, tell Inigo to take a portion

indicators.note: the answer is a portion of the words that come before

explanation.surface: Someone passing on a message about sharing an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a portion' sounds like a serving of food, fitting the surface, but it instructs you to take part of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini are small ring-shaped stuffed pasta from Italy.

clue.text: Meandering topless, provoking reactions

indicators.note: the top letter, in a down answer the first, is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone wandering about half-naked, getting reactions.
explanation.walkthrough: STROLLING loses its first letter. Online trolling means posting to provoke people.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolling is deliberately provoking reactions, especially online.

clue.text: National Trust supported by Everyman: donated, tipped, droned on

indicators.note: the tip, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A heritage charity backed by the setter's donations, and someone drones about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses. Everyman is the setter, so he is I.
explanation.definitionFit: To intonate is to recite in a sing-song or monotone, much like droning on.

clue.text: Mentors giving Bill protection from sun

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Mentors hand someone called Bill a sun hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is capitalised as if a man's name; it is a poster, an AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentors are advisors who guide a less experienced person.

clue.text: Safari's speed?

definitions.meaning: a journey into the bush to see or hunt animals
an old sense of the answer: promptness, the quality of getting things done fast

explanation.surface: A question about how fast a safari goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. Expedition as speed is the older sense, as in expedite.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, and expedition also means promptness or speed.

clue.text: Counterpart of doe or hen

parts.note: the male deer, partner of the female
the male equivalent of a hen party, the night out before a wedding

explanation.surface: A zoology question about the male of two species.
explanation.walkthrough: A buck is the usual partner of a doe and a cock of a hen, but STAG fits both: the male deer, and the stag party that matches a hen party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and a stag night is the groom's counterpart to the bride's hen night.

clue.text: Like water on lake? £1

indicators.note: £1 is placed on, that is after, the lake

explanation.surface: Someone asks what water on a lake is worth: a pound?
explanation.walkthrough: £1 is read as 'one quid', giving I QUID; quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the standard liquid, so 'like water' is liquid.

clue.text: Unusual powerful chesspiece, itself taking its own knight

indicators.note: the knight is taken off the board, so N is removed

parts.note: QUEEN without N, the chess symbol for knight
the queen itself: R, for Regina
the N inside the queen's own name is the piece captured and removed

explanation.surface: A chess oddity: a queen capturing a knight of her own colour.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the chess notation for a knight, so the queen taking its own knight loses its N. R is Regina, the queen herself, as in ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its old sense means strange or unusual.

clue.text: Duck, ablaze: this bird's brightly coloured

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: A duck on fire, and a remark on which bird is bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' pretends to be the bird, but it is a nought, O. The clue writes O first, but the answer needs FLAMING first; the colon lets the two sit in either order. The pink colour of 'this bird' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a bird famous for its bright pink plumage.

clue.text: Nasty and small, the wherewithal

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Something both nasty and small, but necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean and small' also suggests stinginess, the opposite of having the wherewithal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone with the means to buy a house has the money, the wherewithal, to do it.

clue.text: Against — alternately, 'gainst — independence

indicators.note: alternately means every other one in turn, so you take the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone opposing independence in a dialect way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternately' looks like 'in other words' and ''gainst' like a mere restatement of the definition; it is letter fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix used as a word: to be anti something is to be opposed to it.

clue.text: In which squiffy or tight men fear retribution, finally?

definitions.text: In which squiffy or tight men fear retribution, finally?

indicators.note: squiffy means drunk, so the letters are jumbled
finally means at the end, so only the last letter of retribution is used

explanation.surface: Drunken men dread the payback that comes with the hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as spelling it: after a night out, tight (drunk) men fear the day's retribution. Squiffy and tight are both British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning after is the hungover morning following a night of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Runs over, sits back for Alpine dish

indicators.note: sits back is read literally: the word SITS turned back to front

parts.note: used as itself, then written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone recaps a cricket match and settles back to eat Swiss food.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs, over and sits back read like a cricket scorecard and a rest, but each is a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosti is a Swiss potato cake, a dish of the Alps.

clue.text: Less important songs lacking energy as well

indicators.note: lacking means going without something

explanation.surface: A remark on minor tracks that also lack energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The B-side was the second track on a single, usually the lesser song.
explanation.definitionFit: Music-industry term: the B-side of a single held the lesser track, the hit going on the A-side.
